summary:
Public Law 118-232, enacted January 4, 2025, repeals Section 12 of Public Law 98-213 (codified at 48 U.S.C. 1662a) to restore the ability of the people of American Samoa to approve amendments to the territorial constitution based on majority rule in a democratic act of self-determination. The Act's operative mechanism is the repeal of the specified statutory provision, thereby removing the federal restriction on amendments to or modifications of the Constitution of American Samoa.

By repealing 48 U.S.C. 1662a, the Act eliminates the requirement for further congressional action to approve amendments to the territorial constitution. The authority for this delegation of administration of federal territorial law is rooted in an Act of Congress delegating such administration to the President, and subsequently to the Secretary of the Interior under Executive Order 10264 (dated June 29, 1951). Under this framework, the Constitution of American Samoa was originally approved and may now be amended without further congressional action, subject to the plenary authority of Congress under the Territorial Clause (Article IV, Section 3, Clause 2 of the United States Constitution). 

The Act contains no new authorizations of appropriations, nor does it establish new federal agencies, programs, or regulatory mandates. It is strictly a repeal of an existing statutory restriction. The repeal is effective as of the date of enactment, January 4, 2025. There are no material exceptions, conditions precedent, or sunset provisions included in the enacted text.
